No fatal defect found in these 3 items.

Item-by-item result:

- **`thm-fitting-subgroup-of-the-frattini-quotient`** — Statement is true as written. The inclusion `F(G)/Φ(G) ≤ F(G/Φ(G))` follows because `F(G)/Φ(G)` is normal and nilpotent in `G/Φ(G)`; the reverse inclusion is valid: pulling back `F(G/Φ(G))` gives `N ⊴ G` with `Φ(G) ≤ N`, `N/Φ(G)` nilpotent, so `[L3]` lifts nilpotence to `N`, and `[L1]` gives `N ≤ F(G)`. The dependencies `[L1]–[L4]` are restated faithfully. Trivial group boundary: all groups degenerate to the trivial group and the equality holds.

- **`thm-order-of-automorphism-group-of-elementary-abelian-rank-two`** — Statement is true. The proof correctly establishes the automorphism criterion: a homomorphism is determined by the images `u,v` of the coordinate generators; it is an automorphism iff `u ≠ 0` and `v ∉ ⟨u⟩`; the bad cases give a proper image, while the good cases give `p` disjoint cosets of size `p`, hence all `p²` elements and surjectivity, and finite surjection gives bijection. The count `(p²−1)(p²−p)` is correct. The `p = 2` boundary gives `6`, correct. Dependency restatements `[L1]–[L8]` match the reproduced texts.

- **`thm-groups-of-order-p-squared-q-have-a-normal-sylow-subgroup`** — Statement is true. For `p > q`, `n_p | q` and `n_p ≡ 1 (mod p)` force `n_p = 1`. For `q > p`, `n_q ∈ {1, p²}` because the divisor `p` is excluded by congruence; `n_q = p²` forces `p² ≡ 1 (mod q)`, hence `q | p²−1`, and the arithmetic correctly reduces to the sole exceptional pair `(p,q) = (2,3)`. The order-twelve boundary is handled correctly: if `n_3 = 4`, the four Sylow 3-subgroups contribute eight nonidentity elements, leaving exactly four elements; every Sylow 2-subgroup has order 4 and cannot contain an order-3 element, so it is that four-element complement, hence unique and normal. Dependencies `[L1]` and `[L2]` are restated faithfully.

Coverage:
- Read all three items fully, including proof contracts and boundary rows.
- Read all reproduced dependency title/claim sections and checked the `[L#]` restatements against them; no mismatch found.
- Boundary cases instantiated: trivial group for the Fitting/Frattini item; `p = 2` for the automorphism-count item; the exceptional order-twelve case and both prime orderings for the Sylow item. No `n=0` or empty-family case is applicable to any of the three claims.
- Minor terseness in `step 3.1` of the first item and `step 4.1` of the third is not a mathematical defect; the substantive steps carry the proof.
